items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: Zilver Randolph, who later I met in Chicago, in the '30s after I became a musician myself. However, I worked for him in Chicago.

ctx.x: Well, food shows -- food contests -- they would bake pies and cakes, and have it on the banquet table down in the everyone would center, and they'd dance around. Now, the two bands -- leading bands at that time that were stationed in Kansas City was George E. Georgie Lee, who had a sister named Julia Lee. She sang, and later she formed a combo of her own and recorded out of here for Capitol. Benny Moten Benny Morton. Benny had a hell of a band. He wasn't a taskmaster, but he had a good band. I liked his band…

Anyway, during my stay in Kansas City from -- let's see, '25 to '29, bands came through there such as the McKinney Cottonpickers, Zach Jack Whyte, Jack Allen's Cottonpickers, the Blues Serenaders, the Rice Brothers from Milwaukee, Zilver Randolph, who later I met in Chicago, in the '30s after I became a musician myself. However, I worked for him in Chicago.

Who else came through there? Oh. Barron Lee. It was a band out of, say, something like the Southern part of the South. I don't know exactly which state. Then there was Carmite Thompson, who was a trumpet player out of Dallas, Texas. He was a rather young man. And these bands I heard constantly, like, weekends on the domestics' nights off.
